finding: With no owner record, the text gives no rule for the branch `create-worktree --name` would create, and step 4's only rule ('filled from git.branch-template') is wrong for some templates.
why: create-worktree fills the template only when it holds a placeholder other than `{user}`, fills `{user}` with the git user name, and else uses `worktree-<name>`; an agent that fills the template with the work id names a branch that does not exist, so the reason names no branch and the retry stops again at step 4 with 'branch exists'.
fix: State the script's rule at this point (a template with a placeholder other than `{user}` is filled, `{user}` with the git user name; else `worktree-<work id, lower-cased>`), or point at the `--name` paragraph of the `scripts/create-worktree` header.
evidence: SKILL.md:34 "Else it is the branch step 4's `create-worktree --name <work id, lower-cased>` would create, named only when it exists."; scripts/create-worktree:30-31 "the branch is `git.branch-template` with `{name}` and `{user}` filled when it holds no other placeholder, else `worktree-<name>`"; branch_for_name at scripts/create-worktree:249-258

finding: With no owner record, the reason tells the person to delete the template-filled branch even when that branch holds a committed `DIAGNOSIS.md` that step 4 would resume as a re-run.
why: State: a worktree folder `<work id>` with no record on another branch, and the template-filled branch left by an earlier diagnose run with its diagnosis committed; step 4 would cut a worktree onto that branch, so the retry does not need it gone, yet the text says it does and names `git branch -D` for it.
fix: Name the template-filled branch for deletion only when it holds no `DIAGNOSIS.md` for this Work id naming it as the Diagnosis branch (the same test step 4 applies).
evidence: SKILL.md:34 "A retry needs that folder, that record and that branch gone. ... then `git branch -D <named branch>` when a branch is named and still exists."; SKILL.md:35 "A refusal naming the branch as existing is a re-run whose worktree is gone only when a `DIAGNOSIS.md` for this Work id names that branch as its Diagnosis branch, committed on it ...: cut one onto that branch"

finding: The 2 new autopilot journal lines use an event and a subject outside the journal grammar, and the plain-terms clause carries finding ids.
why: `done` is not an autopilot event, `—` is not a subject, and 'rebased onto ...' has no event token; 'f060 and f061' is not followable by a reader without workflow vocabulary.
fix: Use a listed autopilot event and subject (for example `run`), or record the token in JOURNAL-FORMAT.md in the same commit; replace the finding ids with their plain meaning.
evidence: JOURNAL-FORMAT.md:25 "`{subject}` — a subtask id (`NNNN-slug`), `run`, `gate`, or `understanding`."; :34 autopilot events "`run start ...`; `heartbeat ...`; `parked({status})`; `park-inherited(...)`; `stranded`; `run end (...)`"; JOURNAL.md:82-83 "| autopilot | 0005-bug-mode | done — ..." / "| autopilot | — | rebased onto origin/main 3c6bd7c ... with the human's call on f060 and f061"
